title: Satchin Panda Resigns From Salk Institute After Misconduct Allegations
excerpt: The Indian-American circadian biology pioneer, one of the world's most cited scientists, will step down on August 13 after a female research assistant filed a workplace misconduct complaint.
body:
Satchidananda "Satchin" Panda, an Indian-American chronobiologist recognized globally for his pioneering research on circadian rhythms and intermittent fasting, has resigned from the Salk Institute for Biological Studies in La Jolla, California, after a female research assistant raised allegations of sexual misconduct.

Panda will formally leave his post on August 13, the journal Science reported, ending a 22-year tenure at one of the world's most prestigious biological research institutes. He had been placed on administrative leave while the Salk Institute investigated the complaint.

Investigation and Response

According to a statement from the Salk Institute, a staff research assistant raised concerns about workplace misconduct through official reporting channels in March 2026.

"The Institute offered support and resources to the staff member and initiated a prompt, thorough, and impartial investigation."

— Salk Institute, official statement

The identity of the complainant has not been disclosed. According to media reports, the woman later voluntarily left the institute. The Salk Institute has not revealed whether the investigation reached any formal findings before Panda's departure was announced.

Panda denied the allegations in an email cited by Science, writing that he is "deeply committed to maintaining a safe, respectful, and professional environment for everyone in my research team and across the Institute." In a separate communication to colleagues, he said his resignation was motivated by plans to write a book on how recent advances in circadian rhythm research could transform human health.

"This is the right moment to pause, take fresh stock of these shifts, and redefine the goals for the next phase of my career," he reportedly told lab members, according to The Federal.

A Career Built on Circadian Science

Panda's laboratory focused on understanding how the body's internal 24-hour clock influences metabolism, sleep, and chronic diseases. His work on time-restricted eating — a form of intermittent fasting where meals are consumed within a set 8-to-12-hour window — attracted widespread public attention and millions of dollars in research funding for the Salk Institute.

He authored two popular books on circadian health and was named to Clarivate's Highly Cited Researchers list, placing him among the world's most influential scientists by publication impact. In 2023, the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) elected him a Fellow, and in 2025, his team was named a semifinalist in the $101 million XPRIZE Healthspan competition.

According to Science, Panda has not been seen on the Salk campus for several weeks.

Pattern of Misconduct Allegations at Salk

Panda's departure has drawn comparisons to the 2018 resignation of Inder Verma, another Indian-origin scientist at the Salk Institute. Verma, a prominent cancer biologist, stepped down after eight women — six of them affiliated with the institute — accused him of sexual harassment spanning four decades. Verma also denied the allegations.

The earlier case triggered broader scrutiny of the institute's handling of misconduct complaints. Three female Salk professors had separately filed gender discrimination lawsuits in 2017, alleging inequities in grants, promotions, and salaries compared to male counterparts.

Implications for Indian Scientists Abroad

Panda's case is being closely watched within Indian scientific and diaspora communities, where he had become a prominent public figure through his research and bestselling books. For Indian-origin researchers at elite American institutions, the episode underscores the growing accountability frameworks around workplace conduct in academia — standards that have intensified since the broader #MeToo reckoning in scientific institutions.

What Comes Next

The Salk Institute has not disclosed further details about the investigation or its outcome. Panda's formal departure date of August 13 leaves open questions about the status of ongoing research projects and grants tied to his laboratory, including the XPRIZE Healthspan competition entry. The institute's handling of the case will likely face continued scrutiny given its history with the Verma controversy eight years ago.
